name: codyte-spawn-optimized-agents
description: Universal cross-tool swarm orchestrator. Decomposes a /goal into isolated parallel sub-agents (file-partition isolation, no conflicts), spawns them, collects concise feedback, and runs a final review pass until the goal is done. Auto-loads a Codyte profile for c:\Server_Dev.
author: Carlos Ortiz
isolation: file-partition (disjoint scope per agent; no merge step)
spawn: auto-detect (native Agent tool in Claude Code; `claude` CLI otherwise)
subordinate_spawn: claude CLI (for now); native Agent tool when orchestrator is Claude Code

profiles.generic: core lifecycle only; no Codyte constraints

efficiency_engine.shape: Strong brain plans + reviews; cheap hands execute. Opus-over-Haiku, never Haiku-over-Opus.
efficiency_engine.step_a_swarm_or_not: 1-2 independent slices (or mostly serial) => do NOT swarm, run inline. 3+ truly parallel => swarm.
efficiency_engine.cost_order_that_matters: fewer/larger agents > native tool over CLI > cheaper worker model > less output

cost_levers.note: Measured: CLI-spawn cost is ~84% cold-start cache, ~16% output. Order by real impact.
cost_levers.1_native_tool: Use the native Agent tool in Claude Code — kills per-spawn cold-start (~450-525k cache tokens/spawn). Biggest lever. Tradeoff: no per-agent token breakdown.
cost_levers.2_cheaper_model: Haiku ~3.7x cheaper than Sonnet for comparable work; use for mechanical agents.
cost_levers.3_fewer_agents: Each spawn pays the fixed cold-start once; don't over-partition small goals.
cost_levers.4_minimize_output: Real but smallest share in spawn mode — optimize last.

conflict_guard: Before spawning, no path may appear in more than one agent's scope.txt. Overlap => merge agents or sequence via dependency.
